correctness.rationale: The weighted-tree transport cut formula yields κ(xy)=2(p_x(y)+p_y(x))−2; summing over m edges gives total 2 and excludes k>2/m. For arbitrary nonsymmetric weights normalized by min=1, central t and leaf totals X≥a, Y≥b max(1,kt/(2−kb)) imply a strictly increasing scalar necessary condition Φ_{a,b,k}(t)≥k, whose unique sharp root is the two-branch T_{a,b}(k). At k*=4/[2b+1+sqrt(1+4a(b+1))] the active inequality changes. Explicit leaf weights 1 and B=max(1,kT/(2−kb)) attain the bound; equality and strict monotonicity force the unique normalized profile. Endpoint checks T(0)=sqrt(ab), T(2/m)=b+1 and boundary k*=2/m iff a=b. Independent numerical curvature checks support but do not replace this proof.
